description: ADR-0020 §7: least-privilege capability for the Tauri + Python Sidecar migration. Every permission is explicit (Tauri v2 ships zero permissions by default). Permissions granted: (1) core window/event/webview defaults for the main + bubble windows; (2) shell:allow-spawn + kill + stdin-write — the spawn permission is scoped to ONLY the python-sidecar binary via plugins.shell.scope in tauri.conf.json (Tauri v2 enforces BOTH the capability permission AND the config scope at runtime, so the per-triple binary names live in tauri.conf.json's shell.scope, not here — see ADR-0020 §7's `allow` list which is realized by that scope); (3) notification + clipboard-manager + dialog for the toast/paste/export paths; (4) the tauri-plugin-single-instance gate does NOT require a capability grant — it is a non-scoped plugin registered via `.plugin(tauri_plugin_single_instance::init(...))` in main.rs (ADR-0020 §7 + Phase 4 — the second instance is routed to focus the first window instead of launching a duplicate). Tray: the Python sidecar owns the tray via pystray (no Tauri-mode branch needed; the sidecar inherits the desktop session from externalBin spawn), so no core:tray:* permissions are granted to the Rust host. FT-1 full-app relaunch uses AppHandle::restart() (core tauri crate, no plugin required), so no process:allow-restart capability is needed. ADR-0020 §15: tauri-plugin-updater is intentionally NOT granted any permissions — auto-update is out of scope for v1 (see docs/migration/signing-guide.md §'No auto-update').
